cases.task: Handle a customer whose team was locked out mid-shift by a failed renewal
cases.question: Tell me about a time a customer was upset with you or your company. What did you do?
cases.expected_signal: Acts on how the customer feels before explaining what went wrong.
evaluation_criteria: Names what they learned or changed
cases.answer: Last winter a customer called about a failed renewal and she was near tears — her whole team was locked out mid-shift. I said I could hear it had landed badly and that before anything else I'd get her team back in. I issued a seven-day grace extension while we sorted the card, confirmed access with her on the line, and only then walked through why the payment failed. She emailed the next day to say it was the calmest support call she'd had. What I took from it is that the order matters: access first, explanation second.

cases.task: Diagnose a vague report of the dashboard not loading
cases.question: Walk me through how you'd diagnose a customer who says the dashboard 'isn't loading'.
cases.expected_signal: Splits the problem space before guessing, and knows when to stop.
cases.answer: I'd start with what changed — 'was it working yesterday?' — because that splits the space fastest. Then browser and device, then the exact wording on screen, then whether it's just them or the whole team. I narrate as I go: 'I'm asking because it tells me whether this is your account or all of them.' If I can't reproduce it in ten minutes and there's an error id, it goes to engineering with the steps written out.

cases.question: A customer asks for a refund two days outside the policy window. How do you handle it?
cases.expected_signal: Weighs the reason against the rule and knows the limit of their own authority.
evaluation_criteria: Looks at the reason before the rule

cases.answer: I'd look at their account history and why they missed the window. If it seemed genuine I'd try to get it approved, and if I couldn't approve it myself I'd take it to my manager and let the customer know what I was doing.
cases.notes: Two criteria clearly evidenced, the third only implied. The middle of the scale is where a scoring engine earns its keep — anyone can identify the extremes.
